subject: Trickling Down Input Through a Number of Modules

messages.author: 1200926c1d8c4eb2
messages.subject: Trickling Down Input Through a Number of Modules
parts:
I have an application where I ask the user for some input then I take the input and process it in a module and display some output (let's call it module 1), then I take the output of module 1 and process it in another module and display some output (call it module 2). I expected that when the input change, the change will trickle down to module 2, but this is not the case. 

What am I doing wrong?


Simplified Code:

library(shiny)

mod1UI <- function(id){
  ns <- NS(id)
  tagList(
    textInput(ns("txtIn"), "Enter Your Text:", "My Text"),
    uiOutput(ns("txtOut"))
  )
}
mod1 <- function(input, output, session){
  output$txtOut <- renderUI(
    h2(input$txtIn)
    )
  return(reactive(session$ns(input$txtIn)))
}

mod2UI <- function(id){
  ns <- NS(id)
  tagList(
    uiOutput(ns("txtOut"))
  )
}
mod2 <- function(input, output, session, prevModReturn){
  output$txtOut <- renderUI(
    h2(prevModReturn)
  )
  return(reactive(session$ns(prevModReturn)))
}

ui <- fluidPage(
  fluidRow(
    column(12,
           tagList(
             mod1UI("myMod1"),
             mod2UI("myMod2"),
             mod2UI("myMod3"),
             mod2UI("myMod4")
           )
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  mod1return <- callModule(mod1, "myMod1")
  mod2return <- callModule(mod2, "myMod2", mod1return())
  mod3return <- callModule(mod2, "myMod3", mod2return())
  mod4return <- callModule(mod2, "myMod4", mod3return())
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

Two things:

  1. The bug that I think you're looking for is that you're calling the functions modXreturn inside the callModule() call, instead of in the module server function. So if you change that, you'll see the trickling down you're expecting. Here's the working code (differences highlighted):

1. library(shiny)

    mod1UI <- function(id){
      ns <- NS(id)
      tagList(
        textInput(ns("txtIn"), "Enter Your Text:", "My Text"),
        uiOutput(ns("txtOut"))
      )
    }
    mod1 <- function(input, output, session){
      output$txtOut <- renderUI(
        h2(input$txtIn)
      )
      return(reactive(session$ns(input$txtIn)))
    }

    mod2UI <- function(id){
      ns <- NS(id)
      tagList(
        uiOutput(ns("txtOut"))
      )
    }
    mod2 <- function(input, output, session, prevModReturn){
      output$txtOut <- renderUI(

1.     h2(prevModReturn())
      )
      return(reactive(session$ns(prevModReturn())))

1. }

    ui <- fluidPage(
      fluidRow(
        column(12,
          tagList(
            mod1UI("myMod1"),
            mod2UI("myMod2"),
            mod2UI("myMod3"),
            mod2UI("myMod4")
          )
        )
      )
    )

    server <- function(input, output) {
      mod1return <- callModule(mod1, "myMod1")

1.   mod2return <- callModule(mod2, "myMod2", mod1return)
      mod3return <- callModule(mod2, "myMod3", mod2return)
      mod4return <- callModule(mod2, "myMod4", mod3return)

1. }

    shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

1. This is a pretty fundamental concepts in modules and it seems to trip up a lot of people. The secret with modules is never passing actual values (in your case, the return value of the  modXreturn function), but passing in the recipe itself (in your case, the modXreturn function itself). If you pass in a value, it will never update again. If you pass in a (reactive) recipe, it will update properly.

1. Are you sure you're doing what you want to do? You said:

    "I take the input and process it in a module and display some output (let's call it module 1), then I take the output of module 1 and process it in another module"

1. But what you're doing above is taking the input, process it in a module and display the output (so far so good), then taking the input (not the output, like you said) and re-process it from scratch in another module. You're also using the session$ns() function in a strange way. This is usually used when you're creating dynamic inputs on the module server function. If you're just passing already-existing inputs, you don't need it... In your case, literally the only effect it is having is concatenating the module id to the string... If you don't want that, just take that out:

      )
    }

      )
1.   return(reactive(input$txtIn))

    }

      )
      return(reactive(prevModReturn()))

1. }

    ui <- fluidPage(
      fluidRow(
        column(12,
          tagList(
            mod1UI("myMod1"),
            mod2UI("myMod2"),
            mod2UI("myMod3"),
            mod2UI("myMod4")
          )
        )
      )
    )

    server <- function(input, output) {
      mod1return <- callModule(mod1, "myMod1")

1.   mod2return <- callModule(mod2, "myMod2", mod1return)
      mod3return <- callModule(mod2, "myMod3", mod2return)
      mod4return <- callModule(mod2, "myMod4", mod3return)

1. }

    shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

1. More importantly though, if your goal is to process things in chunks (each module is responsible for a step of the processing), this is not accomplishing it, because you're just passing in the same unaltered input every time. This is what I think you were looking for:

    mod1UI <- function(id){
      ns <- NS(id)
      tagList(
        textInput(ns("txtIn"), "Enter Your Text:", "My Text"),
        uiOutput(ns("txtOut"))
      )
    }
    mod1 <- function(input, output, session){

1.   processedTxt <- reactive({
        h2(input$txtIn)
      })
      
      output$txtOut <- renderUI(
        processedTxt()
      )
      return(processedTxt)

1. }

    mod2UI <- function(id){

      tagList(
        uiOutput(ns("txtOut"))
      )
    }
    mod2 <- function(input, output, session, prevModReturn){

1.   processedTxt <- reactive({

      })
      
      output$txtOut <- renderUI(
        processedTxt()
      )
      return(processedTxt)
    }

    mod3UI <- function(id){

1.   ns <- NS(id)
      tagList(
        uiOutput(ns("txtOut"))
      )
    }

1. mod3 <- function(input, output, session, prevModReturn){
      processedTxt <- reactive({
        tags$div(prevModReturn(), style = "color: red")
      })
      
      output$txtOut <- renderUI(
        processedTxt()
      )
      return(processedTxt)

1. }

    ui <- fluidPage(
      fluidRow(
        column(12,

            mod1UI("myMod1"),
